cve_summary: The bad_mode function in arch/arm64/kernel/traps.c in the Linux kernel before 3.9.5 on the ARM64 platform allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) via vectors involving an attempted register access that triggers an unexpected value in the Exception Syndrome Register (ESR).
commit_message:
arm64: don't kill the kernel on a bad esr from el0

Rather than completely killing the kernel if we receive an esr value we
can't deal with in the el0 handlers, send the process a SIGILL and log
the esr value in the hope that we can debug it. If we receive a bad esr
from el1, we'll die() as before.

Signed-off-by: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
docstring:
Summary: This code fragment defines several functions related to system call handling and error reporting in a kernel environment.

Parameters: 
do_ni_syscall:
  regs (struct pt_regs *): pointer to the register state of the current task.
bad_mode:
  regs (struct pt_regs *): pointer to the register state when a bad mode is detected.
  reason (int): reason code for the bad mode.
  esr (unsigned int): exception syndrome register value.
__pte_error:
  file (const char *): name of the source file where the error occurred.
  line (int): line number of the error.
  val (unsigned long): value of the bad page table entry.
__pmd_error:
  file (const char *): name of the source file where the error occurred.
  line (int): line number of the error.
  val (unsigned long): value of the bad page middle directory.
__pgd_error:
  file (const char *): name of the source file where the error occurred.
  line (int): line number of the error.
  val (unsigned long): value of the bad page global directory.
trap_init:
  N/A

Returns: 
do_ni_syscall: long - returns the result of the syscall or an error code.
bad_mode: None - handles an error without returning a value.
__pte_error: None - logs an error without returning a value.
__pmd_error: None - logs an error without returning a value.
__pgd_error: None - logs an error without returning a value.
trap_init: None - initializes traps without returning a value.

Logic: The `do_ni_syscall` function checks for compatibility mode and logs unhandled signals before returning a not-implemented syscall error. The `bad_mode` function handles exceptions by logging critical information and notifying the system of the error. The error functions log specific bad entries in the page table, middle directory, or global directory
